title: Curriculum

profile.name: Luiz Felipe Couto Gontijo
profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer · Games Engineering MSc student

summary: Computer Science graduate from the Federal University of Minas Gerais (UFMG), currently working as a Senior Software Engineer and doing a Master's degree in Games Engineering at the University of Warwick. I'm passionate about software development, always looking to learn new technologies, meet new people and new areas of innovation.

experience.description: Started on the messaging backend, building high-efficiency solutions with Redis, Websockets and related technologies. Moved to the developer experience team, building tools to improve the efficiency, standardization and capabilities of other engineering teams (GitHub Actions, CI/CD, OpenAPI — mostly TypeScript and Go). Currently working on the core backend infrastructure of the platform: message exchanging protocols, Kafka, authentication and more.

Worked at Yalo as a contractor before being hired full-time. Maintained and developed backend APIs, networking and messaging services using Kafka, Redis, Websockets, Kubernetes and GCloud, focusing on maintainability, efficiency and scalability.

Started as a Golang developer on a service mesh manager, working heavily with Kubernetes, Docker and cloud computing. From mid-2022, worked as a full stack developer on a brand new product using Node.js, TypeScript and React.
Main developer of a React Native app for easy evaluation of item samples for industries, built with React Native, Node.js and TypeScript. Also worked as a full stack developer on the main website.

education.description: Understanding and implementing a graphics engine from the ground up: rasterization, rendering, ray tracing and path tracing, with 2D and 3D projects in C++ and DirectX. Game development with individual and group projects using our own engine, Unreal Engine and Godot.
Projects on low-level topics in C and C++, data science in Python and compilers with LLVM. Final grade: 83%.
education.thesis: High-Performance Implementation of the Irregular Wavefront Propagation Pattern on GPU using Gunrock — parallel and efficient IWP algorithms implemented first in Rust, then in C++/CUDA on GPU using the Gunrock graph library.
